_meta: Externally-researched circuit-optimization techniques injected into Aristotle prompts by gen_prompts.py. Techniques are candidate ideas from the ZK literature — the Clean challenge is R1CS with cost = allocations + constraints, so some lookup/GKR/sumcheck tricks may NOT map; Aristotle must verify applicability before use. Refreshed periodically via web research.
_common: MECHANICAL POST-PASS over the finished constraint system (arkworks r1cs-optimizer passes): (a) DEAD VARIABLE ELIMINATION — drop every allocated witness never read by a surviving constraint; (b) CONSTRAINT DEDUPLICATION — identical rank-1 rows collapse to one; (c) CONSTANT FOLDING; (d) LINEAR SUBSTITUTION — a variable defined by an affine constraint is inlined into its uses and both it and its defining row disappear. Cost here is allocations+constraints, so each pass pays twice; run this sweep at the END of any rewrite, since hand-golfing reliably leaves orphaned witnesses behind.

GAUSSIAN-ELIMINATION DISTILLING (Albert et al., CAV 2022, 'Distilling Constraints in Zero-Knowledge Protocols', implemented in circom): run Gaussian elimination over the NON-LINEAR constraint set to DEDUCE previously implicit LINEAR constraints, then use those to substitute away variables and delete rows — strictly stronger than plain linear substitution, because it finds linear facts implied only by the quadratic rows. Reported up to 16.33% of constraints removed from circomlib circuits that had ALREADY been hand-simplified — assume a hand-golfed circuit still hides redundancy, and re-run this after every rewrite. HOW TO ACTUALLY RUN IT (circom --O2 mechanics, docs.circom.io/circom-language/circom-insight/simplification): collect the MAXIMAL CLUSTERS of linear constraints that share signals and solve each cluster in one go with a lazy Gauss-Jordan pass, rather than substituting one row at a time; then iterate to FIXPOINT — after substitution some constraints that were non-linear BECOME linear, so repeat rounds until no eliminable linear constraint remains. SCOPING RULE: only a constraint containing at least one PRIVATE signal may be eliminated; interface inputs/outputs are fixed by the challenge and can never be substituted away. IN CLEAN THIS IS CONCRETE: any value you `witness` that is an AFFINE function of values already in scope is pure waste — affine combinations are free Expressions here, so inline it and delete its assertEq. That removes 1 allocation AND 1 constraint, i.e. 2 units of score per elimination. Do this sweep LAST, after the circuit shape is final, and re-prove the affected theorems.

CLEAN STRUCTURING IDIOM (zksecurity, 'Verifying Poseidon in Clean'): wrap each repeated block in its OWN FormalCircuit and drive it with Circuit.foldl instead of unfolding every iteration inline — unfolding makes the elaborated term enormous and elaboration 'slow and brittle', which is the usual reason an aggressive rewrite cannot close its proofs and ends up returning `sorry`. Applies directly to all five challenges: 64 SHA-256 rounds, 24 Keccak rounds, the 17 RSA squarings/multiplies, the per-bit scalar-mul ladder. Conversely keep CHEAP AFFINE work (round constants, linear/matrix layers) INLINE — factoring it into its own circuit obscures the proof without lowering cost. localLength must account for EVERY intermediate witness, so count per-iteration allocations exactly (Poseidon reference: 6 per partial round vs 8 per full round) — that count IS half the score.

NAMED DEAD END — THE GNARK EMULATED-ARITHMETIC SPEEDUPS DO NOT APPLY HERE (checked against ivokub's writeup and the gnark std/algebra approach). All three of their constraint-count wins for non-native multiplication need a prover-verifier CHALLENGE that this cost model does not give you: (a) checking p_y(Z) = p_k(Z)*p_q(Z) by evaluating at random points instead of decomposing limbs — needs Fiat-Shamir randomness; (b) the log-derivative trick F'(Z)/F(Z) = S'(Z)/S(Z) — needs r = Commit({s_i},{e_i}); (c) augmented Groth16 with Pedersen commitments on witness limbs used as the challenge — needs a modified verifier. zkGolf checks a PLAIN R1CS with no commitment or Fiat-Shamir machinery, so none of it is available: you must still pay for the limb carries and range checks. If a paper's speedup rests on a random challenge, a commitment, a lookup argument, GKR or sum-check, it is out of scope here no matter how large the quoted saving.

COMPARISON AGAINST A CONSTANT — WHAT IS AND IS NOT NEW HERE (correcting an earlier note of mine). The weighted-accumulation comparator of Mathematics 13(24):3959 IS circomlib's existing CompConstant: bit PAIRS each contributing a compile-time weight in one quadratic row, with the accumulator sign read off by Num2Bits(135), so its 262 = 127 + 135. Its 759 baseline is a lexicographic comparator, and crucially IT TAKES THE 254 BITS AS INPUT — so it is a comparison optimisation, not a range check, and it is still linear in k. Do not expect a 65% cut on a range check from it. THE GENUINELY USEFUL TRICK FOR x < X WITH X A CONSTANT is Khovratovich's: change only the TOP weight, x = (X - 2^(n-1))*a_(n-1) + sum_(i<=n-2) a_i*2^i, plus n booleanity rows — the two branches overlap and cover exactly [0, X). Exhaustively verified for X = 2..300 and for 1000,1023,1024,1025,4095,5000. Measured at 254 bits: 254 rows and score 507, against Num2Bits(254) + CompConstant(X) at 515 rows and score 1028 — A CLEAN 2x, and circomlib has no such gadget. RELATED: for a plain k-bit range check, DO NOT ALLOCATE THE TOP BIT — define it as the free linear combination (x - sum_(i<k-1) 2^i b_i)/2^(k-1) and apply booleanity to that form, giving k rows + k-1 allocations = 2k-1. circom --O2 does this automatically; arkworks does not and pays 509 instead of 507.

THE SINGLE-ROW NON-VANISHING-MULTIPLIER TRICK (Verified-zkEVM/clean#395) — the general recipe behind the Keccak record, and it transfers to ANY small boolean function, including SHA-256's Ch/Maj/Xor3 (the record's own file notes it was 'ported from Solution.SHA256.Xor3'). Encode the output z in ONE rank-1 row of the shape L1 - (z + L2)*M = 0 where L1, L2, M are AFFINE in the boolean inputs and M is provably NON-ZERO everywhere on the boolean cube. Then the row is linear in z, so z is UNIQUELY pinned — and it inherits booleanity, so NO separate z(z-1)=0 row is needed. Two worked instances: 3-input XOR, (6a + 6b - 24c) - (z + 2a + 2b + 7c)*(a + b - 4c + 1) = 0, multiplier takes only +-1,+-2,+-3 for p > 3; chi = a XOR ((NOT b) AND c), (4a + 2b) - (z + 3a - b - c)*(4a + b + c - 3) = 0, multiplier again +-1,+-2,+-3. Each costs 1 allocation + 1 constraint per bit, HALF the cost of chaining two-input gadgets and with the booleanity row eliminated. To apply it to a new function: pick M affine and nonzero on the cube, then solve for L1, L2 so the row reproduces the truth table; verify M never vanishes (that is what makes z unique).

THE R1CS-NATIVE GATE LIBRARY IS NOT {AND, XOR} — IT IS 192 OF THE 256 THREE-INPUT FUNCTIONS (computed here by exhaustive SMT, cvc5 QF_FF over the circom prime; harness validated on the known XOR3 row). A function f(a,b,c) of boolean inputs is 'native' if it admits ONE rank-1 row L1 - (z + L2)*M = 0 with L1,L2,M affine in a,b,c and M non-vanishing on the cube: z is then uniquely pinned AND inherits booleanity, so the whole gate costs 1 allocation + 1 constraint with NO separate z(z-1)=0 row. FULL CLASSIFICATION: 192 of 256 are native, 64 are not. Every function of GF(2) ANF degree <= 2 is native (all 128 of them). Of the 128 degree-3 functions exactly 64 are native. NATIVE: XOR3, XNOR3, OR3, Maj(a,b,c), Ch(a,b,c), and chi = a XOR ((NOT b) AND c). NOT NATIVE: AND3 = abc, and 63 other degree-3 functions. NOTE THE INVERSION: the 3-input AND — the canonical 'one gate' of the multiplicative-complexity world — CANNOT be done in one row, while XOR3 and chi can. CONSEQUENCE, AND THIS IS THE POINT: a netlist minimised for AND-count under the free-XOR assumption (Bristol Fashion, Boyar-Peralta XAG synthesis, anything from the garbled-circuit or MPC literature) is optimal for a DIFFERENT basis and is NOT optimal here. Do not port such a circuit gate-for-gate. Re-synthesise the algorithm over the native library: cost = the number of MATERIALISED non-affine values, where each materialised value may be ANY of the 192 native functions of three already-materialised bits, and every affine combination in between is free. TO DERIVE THE ROW for a native f: pick an affine M that never vanishes on the cube, then solve the 8 linear equations (f(x) + L2(x))*M(x) = L1(x) for the coefficients of L1 and L2 — with M fixed the system is LINEAR, so this is a small exact solve, not a search.

TENSOR RANK IS THE ROW LOWER BOUND FOR ANYTHING BILINEAR — the single most transferable structural idea. A rank-1 row is EXACTLY one product of two linear forms, and outputs are free linear combinations of row results, so THE MINIMUM NUMBER OF ROWS TO COMPUTE A BILINEAR MAP IS ITS BILINEAR COMPLEXITY (tensor rank). Consequences that are immediately usable: an m-limb by m-limb polynomial product is 2m-1 rows, not m^2, by checking (sum x_i c^i)(sum y_i c^i) = (sum z_i c^i) at the HARD-CODED constants c = 1..2m-1 — both sides are affine in the witnesses because the c^i are constants, there is NO randomness (two degree-(2m-2) polynomials agreeing at 2m-1 points are identical), and 2m-1 is OPTIMAL by Winograd's classical rank result, not merely good; verified in session for m = 2,3,4,8,16 (m=8 gives 15 rows against 64, m=16 gives 31 against 256). A 2x2 matrix product is 7 rows (Strassen), and 7 is a proven lower bound. The whole tensor-rank lower-bound literature — substitution method, Blaser, Winograd — therefore transfers verbatim as R1CS row lower bounds. Reach for this FIRST whenever outputs are bilinear in two groups of inputs.

BOOLEAN-INPUT LOGIC: ROWS SHOULD SCALE WITH INPUT ARITY, NOT OUTPUT COUNT. For ANY number of outputs that are functions of k boolean inputs, allocate the 2^k - k - 1 monomials of degree >= 2 in the bits (each built with one row as monomial x bit); EVERY output is then a FREE linear combination. Verified complete over F_p for k = 2..5. Against circomlib, source-checked: MultiMux3 over n-wide data costs 1 + 6n there against 4 by the monomial basis FOR ANY n; MultiMux4 costs 4 + 16n against 11. SEPARATE AND ALSO USEFUL — THE CONSTANT-TABLE MUX TREE: when the table is CONSTANT the level-0 muxes are T_2j + s0*(T_2j+1 - T_2j), which is AFFINE in s0 and therefore FREE, so only levels 1..k-1 cost anything and a 2^k-entry constant lookup with one output is 2^(k-1) - 1 rows — an 8-entry constant table is 3 rows, not circomlib's 7 (verified for N = 8, 16, 32 on all indices). Use the mux tree for a single output and the monomial basis for several. ALSO WORTH KNOWING: a 2x2 switch costs 1 row + 1 allocation with NO selector bit ((o1-a)(o1-b) = 0 and o2 := a+b-o1 free), so a prover-chosen permutation of n elements via a Waksman network is n*ceil(lg n) - n + 1 rows with no randomness.

PRIOR ART FOR THE SINGLE-ROW TRICK — THE NOVELTY CLAIM SURVIVES, BUT ONLY IN ITS SHARPENED FORM, AND IT HAS A LINEAGE. SPLIT THE CLAIM IN TWO. (1) 'One rank-1 row computes a boolean function and its output is boolean for free' is NOT novel — it is universal and deliberate since 2016 whenever the output is isolated in C and the function has degree <= 2: AND a*b = c; NOR (1-a)(1-b) = c; AND-NOT a(1-b) = c; XOR2 2a*b = a+b-c; Ch (f-g)*e = ch-g; select b(y-x) = y-z; conditional equality a*(b-c) = 0. It is named in the APIs (arkworks new_witness_without_booleanity_check, gnark MarkBoolean) and the Zcash spec says of XOR2 'This automatically boolean-constrains c'. (2) 'Put the output inside a MULTIPLICAND, over a VARIABLE affine multiplier that is a unit on the boolean cube, reaching DEGREE-3 functions with booleanity still free' — no prior art was found for this after an exhaustive sweep. THE HONEST ANTECEDENTS TO CITE: Daira Hopwood's Zcon0 Circuit Optimisation handout (2018, ZcashFoundation/zcon0-workshop-notes, cited by the ZKProof Community Reference as [Hop18]) lists 'merge to do two things at once — merging with boolean constraints in constant comparisons' AND separately the inversion principle with exactly the right side condition ('q*b = a if the inverse exists... what if a = b = 0? then q is unconstrained') — but never composes them, and his n-ary AND still pays a separate booleanity row. Zcash Protocol Spec A.3.2.1 (non-normative) says of unpacking 'it is possible to eliminate it by merging it into the boolean constraint of one of the output bits... we do not use it for the Sapling circuit', and A.3.2.2's constant range check actually deploys it ('the constraints corresponding to zero bits of c are in place of boolean constraints on bits of a_i', Theorem A.3.1). THE STRUCTURAL DIFFERENCE, AND IT IS THE WHOLE POINT: in both Zcash cases the output is recovered by dividing by a CONSTANT (2^-j) and appears in BOTH multiplicands; our form divides by a VARIABLE affine form and keeps the output in ONE multiplicand — that is what buys the extra degree. Closest 2-row analogue: Pinocchio's is-zero, X*M - Y = 0 and (1-Y)*X = 0, where booleanity of Y is IMPLIED by the pair and Y sits inside a multiplicand (arkworks independently exploited this: CHANGELOG 'saved 1 constraint in FpVar::{is_eq, is_neq} by removing the unnecessary booleanity check'). SHARPEST NEGATIVE DATAPOINT: Zcash A.3.2.2's n-ary AND puts the output in a multiplicand across 3 rows and STILL pays an explicit (1-b)b = 0 — precisely where the trick would have applied.

THE ABSENCE OF PRIOR ART HERE IS EVIDENCE, NOT AN ARCHIVE GAP — searched and empty, so do not re-run this survey. XOR3 costs 2 CONSTRAINTS PER BIT in libsnark, bellman, circomlib, bkomuves, arkworks AND gnark: every serious implementation from 2014 to 2025. libsnark's majority_gadget even emits a PURE BOOLEANITY ROW alongside its carry-save row — it must, since x=y=z=0, r=-1/2 satisfies the carry-save row alone. Came up empty: ZKProof Community Reference v0.3 (there is NO academic R1CS gadget cookbook), zkdocs (no R1CS section at all), 0xPARC learn / zk-bug-tracker, docs.circom.io, MoonMath, Vitalik's QAP posts, CirC and Bounded-Verification-for-FF-Blasting (emits w'(w'-1) as a SEPARATE assertion), Distilling Constraints (CAV'22 — explicitly notes 'circuits using bitwise operations leave small room for optimization', and did NOT find circomlib's XOR3 redundancy), Picus/QED2/Coda/AC4/Ecne/Plonkify, the SM3 ZK-circuit paper (Sensors 22(16):5951 — peer-reviewed bit-oriented hash minimization, uses a 2-constraint XOR3 and keeps booleanity separate), ethresear.ch, zkresear.ch, community.zkproof.org, StackExchange. GitHub global code search: '"implies booleanity" OR "booleanity is implied"' -> 0 results; 'xor3 "single constraint" r1cs' -> 0. NO NAME EXISTS for it: 'constraint fusion' is taken (ZKML rounding-merge), 'constraint packing' means batching LINEAR equalities (Zcash A.3.7 BLAKE2s, 7 checks/row), and 'implicit/folded/free booleanity' has zero usage. ONE RESIDUAL GAP, stated honestly: ePrint 2022/462 (Ambrona et al., PlonK arithmetization) is Cloudflare-403 to every tool here; its implementation paper Clap (arXiv:2405.12115) says 'augmented with the information of which variable is boolean [our inlining] can reach one constraint' — but that is about INPUT booleanity as an optimizer hypothesis for 2-input XOR in a degree-2 PlonKish gate, not output-booleanity folding in a rank-1 row. Low risk, not closed.
sha256-hash: CALIBRATION REBUILT FROM ACTUAL CIRCUIT GENERATION (every number below was measured by building the circuit and counting, not quoted). Per ONE 512-bit compression, plain R1CS, no lookups: jsnark 25656 with the constant IV and 25968 generic (variable chaining value) — verified by emitting the real .arith and applying CircuitReader's instruction-to-R1CS mapping; xJsnark claims 25538 (paper Table III, same jsnark->libsnark pipeline, credible but not independently re-measured); bellman 25840 BUT THAT IS A CONSTANT-IV FIRST-BLOCK ARTIFACT — a generic bellman block is 26192 (26166 nonlinear), because with a constant IV the first rounds' ch/maj/rotate-XORs fold away; libsnark 27280 (NOT the widely repeated 27904, which appears in no libsnark file, test or constant and is folklore), rising to 27792 if you count input booleanity, which libsnark deliberately omits (issue #37); arkworks crypto-primitives about 40880 per block, a naive port, not a target; gnark about 25.8k marginal but OUT OF SCOPE and irrelevant anyway, since std/math/uints is built on 2^8 x 2^8 lookup tables plus about 130k fixed table cost. WATCH THE CONVENTION: these differ by whether the 512 message bits' booleanity is counted (jsnark 25392 excluding vs 25968 as measured). Pin that down before claiming a win.

CORRECTION TO AN EARLIER NOTE — THE xJsnark/jsnark CROSS-ROUND Maj SHARING IS REAL BUT IS *NOT* A WIN FOR US, CHECKED. The trick (jsnark README, ~1024 constraints/block): because b_k = a_{k-1} and c_k = a_{k-2}, the product b_k*c_k equals a_{k-1}*b_{k-1}, so alternating the factorization gives 1.5 multiplications per Maj bit instead of 2. That optimizes a TWO-multiplication Maj down to 1.5. We are already at ONE row per Maj bit INCLUDING booleanity via the single-row non-vanishing-multiplier form, and the shared product does not recur under either c + (a+c)(b+c) or (o+a+b-9c+3)(a+b+6c-4) = -12. So 1.5 > 1: importing it is a regression. Recorded so no job spends itself re-deriving it. (An agent did port it into bkomuves' circom and measured 25208 general / 24888 constant-IV, verified against the empty-string vector and 4 random (state, block) pairs — a new public best for plain-R1CS circom, and still above our single-row baseline.)
Majority(B,C,D) = (B&C) ^ (B&D) ^ (C&D): three ANDs + XOR-fold; Ch(E,F,G) = G ^ (E&(F^G)) uses ONE AND (E&(F^G)) instead of two.

Represent each 32-bit word's bits once and reuse; XOR / rotation / shift are FREE affine combinations of bit variables — never allocate constraints for them, only for the AND (booleanity + one rank-1 product).

CALIBRATION, CORRECTED AND MEASURED (the widely-quoted numbers are wrong in two places). bkomuves/hash-circuits' 26170 is labelled 'approximate' in its own README, appears nowhere else, and ships no benchmark harness; compiled here with circom 2.2.3 --O2 it is 26232 general / 26040 constant-IV (budget: rounds 64x294 + 264 = 19080, schedule 48x149 = 7152). libsnark's real figure is 27280 (sha256_gadget.tcc: `return 27280; /* hardcoded for now */`) — THE WIDELY-CITED 27904 IS FOLKLORE, traceable to no primary source. circomlib Sha256compression() = 30328 nonlinear (--O2; 30952 at --O0), Sha256(256) = 29412, Sha256(512) = 59313. bellman = 25840, a hard CI assertion at src/gadgets/sha256.rs:331, constant-IV, so it beats bkomuves' constant-IV 26040 by 200. THE PUBLISHED FRONTIER IS xJsnark's 25538 (Kosba et al., S&P 2018, Table III; Buffet 44999 / Geppetto 38556). ALL of these count NONLINEAR CONSTRAINTS ONLY, with no allocations, so none of them is directly comparable to our allocations+constraints score — and none of them threatens it. Verified-zkEVM/clean's own public Clean/Gadgets/SHA256/ (main branch, NOT PR #395) is about 40280: chained two-operand Add32 at 33 each, written for provability rather than cost. gnark, Noir and arkworks-via-lookups are OUT OF SCOPE (LogUp / plookup / BSB22 commitments).
Carry-save (3:2 compressor) addition to combine the 6-7 addends in the round function before a single final modular reduction, rather than chained 2-input adds.

FREE WIN, UNPUBLISHED, -368 SCORE PER BLOCK: NEVER ALLOCATE THE TOP CARRY BIT OF A DECOMPOSITION — DEFINE IT AS A LINEAR COMBINATION. Every implementation surveyed allocates all 32+ceil(lg k) bits of a sum before truncating (bellman literally allocates then truncate(32)s; bkomuves' Bits35 allocates u, v, w). But once the low bits are allocated, the top bit is already determined by an AFFINE expression in existing witnesses: w := (inp - sum_i 2^i b_i - 2^32 u - 2^33 v) / 2^34. Affine combinations are FREE in R1CS, so w costs ZERO allocations, and w*(1-w) = 0 is ONE row that both pins it boolean and, because w's DEFINITION is the sum-equals-value equation, makes the separate tie row disappear. Net -1 allocation AND -1 constraint per decomposition. Soundness is unchanged: every bit is still boolean, so inp < 2^35 is still pinned. At 184 decompositions per block (see the sharing note) that is -368 score/block, strictly free. GENERALIZES: in ANY range decomposition, allocate only k-1 of the k bits — the last one is an lc — so a k-bit range check costs 2k-1, not 2k.

Smart bitwidth adjustment (xJsnark): track a STATIC upper bound on every intermediate 32-bit word through the adds/XOR-folds and insert a bit-decomposition/normalization ONLY when that bound would overflow the native field — not after every operation. Reported ~3.2k constraints saved vs Geppetto and ~10k vs Buffet on SHA-256; each skipped decomposition removes 32 allocations + its booleanity constraints, so it pays double in this metric.

Global common-subexpression / multivariate-polynomial minimization across the 64 rounds (xJsnark, reported ~8.8k constraints on SHA-256): the message schedule and round function reuse the same sigma/XOR-fold subexpressions — allocate each distinct affine combination ONCE and share it everywhere rather than per-round.

If the framework exposes lookups: 'spread'/interleaved-bit tables (Barretenberg-style) turn XOR3 and Maj into table reads; only worth it if a lookup is cheaper than the ~1 constraint the arithmetic form already costs — verify against this R1CS cost model first.

Boyar-Peralta counter bound also applies to the NATIVE SHA-256 challenge's bit-level adders: MC of Hamming weight of n bits is exactly n - H(n), so multi-operand column addition wants optimal k:log(k) counters, not chained 3:2 compressors. Weigh against the field-arithmetic route here (a native field can add many 32-bit words in one linear combination and range-check once) — pick whichever costs fewer allocations+constraints, but do not assume chained full adders are optimal.

THE SETTLED DECOMPOSITION-SHARING DESIGN IS 184 PER BLOCK, NOT 4 PER ROUND — and circomlib is the outlier that makes it look otherwise. Identical in libsnark, jsnark, xJsnark, bellman and bkomuves: (a) d and h are NEVER decomposed, kept as single field elements (libsnark pack_d/pack_h with enforce_bitness=false); (b) b, c are previous a's and f, g are previous e's, so their bits ALREADY EXIST — never re-decompose; (c) a's bits serve Sigma0 AND Maj, e's bits serve Sigma1 AND Ch, and rotations are re-indexing, free; (d) a schedule word's bits serve sigma0 (read at i+15) and sigma1 (at i+2). Total 64x2 + 48 + 8 = 184 decompositions/block. circomlib pays 4/round by emitting separate BinSum for T1, T2, suma, sume — that single mistake is about +4096/block and explains most of its 30328-vs-26232 gap. If our encoding decomposes more than 184 words per block, that is free score on the table.

THE PREMISE THAT MODULAR REDUCTION DOMINATES THE NATIVE COST IS FALSE — MEASURE BEFORE OPTIMIZING IT. Per-round ledger on the bkomuves basis (294 constraints/round): Sigma0 64 + Sigma1 64 + Ch 32 + Maj 64 = 256, i.e. 87% IS BIT-LOGIC; only 70 (24%) is the two Bits35 modular reductions. So xJsnark's reduction-placement ILP, CirC's encodings and every range-check-shaving idea are fighting over the small quarter. The single-row non-vanishing-multiplier form is the lever that moves the big 87%: it takes that 256 down to 128 rows + 128 allocations. Ledger for a fully-golfed native compression under our allocations+constraints metric: about 35.1k (25216 rounds + 9360 schedule + 520 final) — versus 44430 for the GF(2) variant of the same function.

BLOCK 0's CHAINING VALUE IS THE CONSTANT IV — this challenge hashes a MESSAGE, not a compression with a variable state, so every operation consuming the initial state in block 0 is against compile-time constants and is partially foldable. In the Boolean world that alone is worth -301 ANDs (Goldfeder's sha256Unpadded.txt = 22272 vs Bristol's general 22573; github.com/matteocam/sha256-circuit). In the native world it is the difference between bkomuves' 26232 and 26040. Make sure the first block is specialized and not calling the same generic compression circuit as blocks 1..n.

bellman's MultiEq (src/gadgets/multieq.rs) — PACK SEVERAL INDEPENDENT SUM-EQUALITIES INTO ONE ROW by shifting each by a running bit offset and flushing at the scalar capacity. At 35 bits per equality and BN254's 253-bit capacity that is 7 reductions per row: 184 tie rows collapse to about 27. CAVEAT: this only pays if the framework CHARGES for standalone affine equality rows. If the top-carry-bit-as-lc trick above is applied, the tie rows never exist in the first place and MultiEq is entirely subsumed — check which regime we are in before spending a job on it.
keccak-f1600: DO NOT TRY FIRST/LAST-ROUND SLICING ON THIS CHALLENGE — IT DOES NOT APPLY. For Keccak-256 the last round can be backward-sliced (only 4 output lanes are needed) and the first round benefits from zero capacity lanes, together worth about 3% . But THIS challenge is the RAW PERMUTATION: the interface is state : Vector F 1600 in and state : Vector F 1600 out (same for the K12 instance), so ALL 25 lanes are live outputs and ALL 1600 input bits are free. There is no sponge padding, no capacity, and nothing to slice. Verified against Challenge/Instances/*/Interface.lean.

CALIBRATION AGAINST EVERY PUBLIC PLAIN-R1CS KECCAK — WE ARE ALREADY 1.6x BETTER THAN THE BEST OF THEM. circom keccak-circom/keccak256-circom: about 150848 constraints, because circomlib's XOR3 costs 2 constraints per bit (mid <== b*c; out <== a*(1-2b-2c+4mid)+b+c-2mid) and its chi costs 3. bkomuves/hash-circuits: about 146000 constraints for the permutation. The widely quoted naive breakdown is 7744/round = 185856. Our record is 92160 constraints, and the entire gap is the 1-row XOR3 and 1-row chi gadgets. Anything reported faster than this is out of scope: Keccacheck (eprint 2025/1764) quotes '<4k constraints per instance' but that is the amortised cost of a Groth16 wrapper around a sum-check/GKR proof with random challenges and MLE commitments, not an R1CS encoding; Polyhedra's binary GKR is GKR+sum-check; Binius makes XOR free only by moving to binary tower fields with a different commitment scheme; zkEVM Keccak circuits (Scroll/Polygon/halo2 spread tables) are entirely lookup-based.

ALTERNATIVE STATE REPRESENTATIONS — ALL MEASURED, ALL WORSE (do not spend a slot re-deriving these). (a) PACKED BASE-8 DIGITS, the lookup-free analogue of the 'spread' trick: packing a lane as sum_i 8^i * A[i] is free, and summing 5 lanes gives digit values in [0,5] with no carries — but extracting each parity bit needs C and a quotient q in {0,1,2}, costing 128 allocations + 193 constraints per column-lane = score 321 against the current 256. Worse, because the 1-row XOR3 already handles its carry implicitly and there is no lookup-free way to range-check the digits more cheaply. (b) +/-1 FOURIER BASIS (b -> (-1)^b, XOR becomes multiplication): 3-input parity costs 2 rows instead of 1, 5-input 4 instead of 2 — uniformly about 2x worse, because the boolean encoding is exactly what lets L1/L2/M exploit booleanity. (c) AND-FIRST restructuring (materialise the 1600 chi ANDs and keep everything else GF(2)-linear): 6400 rows/round, because next-state bits become 33-term XORs.

CHI IS AT A PROVEN FLOOR, NOT JUST AN OBSERVED ONE: MC(chi5) = 5 is SAT-PROVED MINIMAL (Ko Stoffelen, 'Optimizing S-box Implementations for Several Criteria using SAT Solvers', FSE 2016, Table 1 — a proven minimum, not an upper bound; same table gives Ascon 5, ICEPOLE 6). Our chi costs 1600 rows/round = 5 rows per 5-bit S-box = exactly that floor, so NO better S-box decomposition exists. Caveat kept honest: a row is strictly more powerful than a GF(2) AND gate (XOR3 is 1 row and 0 ANDs), so MC is a heuristic floor for rows rather than a theorem — but here it is tight. By contrast MC(theta) = 0: every one of theta's 2240 rows/round is pure overhead from GF(2)-linearity not being F_p-linear.

CORRECTION TO AN EARLIER ARGUMENT OF MINE — 'R1CS ROWS ARE FACTORABLE QUADRICS SO ONE EQUATION CANNOT PIN TWO VARIABLES' IS TRUE PER ROW BUT FALSE ACROSS ROWS. The SPAN of two rows' quadratic parts need not split. Explicit counterexample, verified for p = 5,7,11,13,17,19,23,29,31,101,127: row 1 (z1+z2)(z1-z2) = z3 gives z1^2 - z2^2 = z3; row 2 ((d-1)*z2)*z2 = z3 gives (d-1)z2^2 = z3; together z1^2 = d*z2^2 with d a NON-RESIDUE forces z1 = z2 = z3 = 0 uniquely. So TWO rank-1 rows DO pin THREE unknowns. BN254 GOTCHA: p = 1 mod 4, so -1 IS a quadratic residue and x^2 + y^2 = 0 has nontrivial solutions — the least non-residue is 5, so use d in {5,7,10,11,14,15,17,19}. WHY IT STILL DOES NOT HELP, which is the useful part: Chevalley-Warning bounds the prize — r degree-2 rows in m unknowns with sum of degrees < m cannot have exactly one solution, so r >= ceil(m/2) and AT MOST A FACTOR 2 is ever available. And empirically it is not even that: over 1,140,029 sampled affine 3-cubes with uniquely-solvable fibers, two rows never pinned more than ONE affinely-independent function. Structurally, uniqueness with r < m forces the solution to be a singular point, the elimination gives a norm equation whose constant must vanish, and that forces the pinned values to be AFFINE in the inputs — i.e. values that were free anyway. CONCLUSION UNCHANGED, REASONING FIXED: stop looking for sub-one-row-per-non-affine-witness.

FUSING THETA INTO CHI IS IMPOSSIBLE — the open question from an earlier pass is now CLOSED, by a RESTRICTION LEMMA. Lemma: if L1 - (z + L2)*M = 0 encodes f on the boolean cube with L1,L2,M affine and M non-vanishing, then fixing any subset of the inputs to constants gives affine restrictions L1',L2',M' with M' still non-vanishing, encoding f on the subcube. So SINGLE-ROW ENCODABILITY IS CLOSED UNDER SUBCUBE RESTRICTION. Application: the attractive fusion is to skip materialising the 1600 theta outputs and feed chi its pre-XOR inputs, z = chi(a0+d0, a1+d1, a2+d2) = b0 + b2 + b1*b2, which would cost 2560 rows/round (122880 total). Restrict a1 = d1 = 0: then b1 = 0 and f becomes a0 + d0 + a2 + d2, a 4-INPUT XOR of four free variables — which we proved by SMT has no single-row encoding. Contradiction, so the fused gate does not exist. GENERALISATION WORTH REMEMBERING: any single-row gadget whose function restricts on some subcube to a XOR of 4 or more free variables is impossible. Partial fusion (absorbing one D bit into chi's b0 slot only) survives the lemma but is useless, because every theta output bit is consumed in all three chi roles across the five S-boxes of its row and must be materialised anyway.

PROVED WITH SMT — THE SINGLE-ROW XOR STOPS AT 3 INPUTS (cvc5 QF_FF over the circom prime, harness validated against the known 3-input row before trusting the negative results). Question asked: does an n-input XOR admit ONE rank-1 row that pins z uniquely, i.e. L1 - (z + L2)*M = 0 with L1, L2, M affine in the boolean inputs and M non-vanishing on the cube? (This is the fully general single-row shape: a row quadratic in z has two roots and cannot pin z, so z must appear linearly, giving z*M = N with M affine non-vanishing.) PARAMETER TUNING IS EXHAUSTED — FIVE LEVERS CHECKED AND CLOSED (independent cost model reproduced 326297 to within a few percent, so these numbers are trustworthy). (a) KARATSUBA/TOOM IS ALREADY SUBSUMED: checking the product by EVALUATION AT 2m-1 FIXED CONSTANT POINTS, sum x_i c^i * sum y_i c^i = sum z_i c^i, is Toom taken to the maximum, costs 2m-1 rows (Theta(m), below Karatsuba's m^1.58), and interpolation is linear hence FREE. Do not implement Karatsuba. (b) SQUARING SYMMETRY tri(m) = m(m+1)/2 IS WORTHLESS under that scheme — a(c)*a(c) is one row per point exactly like a(c)*b(c); tri(m) only matters in the witness generator. (c) 17 MULTIPLICATIONS IS PROVABLY OPTIMAL: a length-k addition chain reaches at most 2^k and 2^16 < 65537, so l(65537) >= 17; 16 squarings + 1 multiply attains it and windowing cannot help at Hamming weight 2. (d) MERGING SQUARINGS (deferring reduction across steps) IS STRICTLY WORSE: for x^4 in one step the quotient grows to 12288 bits and the total is 26302 bits against 18782 for two separate squarings. (e) LIMB WIDTH IS A FLAT OPTIMUM: the 2mb range-check term is invariant in b, so only the carry term (proportional to b) and the evaluation term (1/b) trade off; b=17 is best and beats our b=24 by only 0.9%. xJsnark found the same plateau.

WHERE THE COST ACTUALLY IS, AND WHY IT IS HARD TO MOVE: about 82% of each modmul is TWO 4096-bit range checks — the quotient q and the remainder r, roughly 8037 rows each at b=24 — with grouped carries about 2627 and the evaluation rows about 1364. THE OBVIOUS ATTACK FAILS FOR TWO INDEPENDENT REASONS. Dropping the quotient range check (letting the carry bounds force q small) is INCOMPATIBLE WITH GROUPED CARRIES: grouping bounds only the group sums, not the individual coefficients, so you would need one carry per coefficient — 12276 bits per op instead of 1368, a net loss of about 21800 against the 8037 saved. It is also UNSOUND for adversarial n: if every limb of n is even, take q0 = 1/2 mod p and every (q*n)_i is a 23-bit value, the carry chain passes, and the circuit accepts a*b - r = n/2. RNS/CRT is likewise dead in plain R1CS — reducing modulo an auxiliary prime needs a witnessed quotient of full bit length, costing at least what it saves; RNS only pays when range checks are lookups. Barrett vs Montgomery is irrelevant because the quotient is nondeterministic advice, so there is no division to optimise. AND THE RANGE CHECK ITSELF IS OPTIMAL: a k-bit check costs 2k-1 (k rows + k-1 allocations) and that is a lower bound — r rank-1 rows cut a variety whose projection has degree at most 2^r by Bezout, so at most 2^r values can be accepted. The top-bit-fold already attains it; base-4 or base-8 digit decompositions tie at best.

MEASURED STATE OF OUR OWN CIRCUIT, SO NOBODY RE-OPTIMISES WHAT IS DONE: PadDigest24 costs Count.zero — the PKCS#1 v1.5 padding check is ALREADY FREE, because the padded block is a constant plus a linear form in the digest bits and constants live in the linear combination (equality against a long CONSTANT is always free in R1CS; only equality between two ALLOCATED values costs a row). It witnesses just 14 split bits for the digest straddling limb boundaries. Remaining small levers, in order: range-check the BYTES rather than the limbs of the modulus and signature (512 x (2*8-1) = 7680 per array against 171 x (2*24-1) = 8037, saving about 357 each, and bytes < 256 implies limbs < 2^24); and b = 24 -> 17 for about 0.9%. Exponent 65537 = 2^16 + 1: exactly 16 squarings + 1 multiply; every step is a fixed-modulus modmul — share reduction machinery across all 17.
Fixed modulus: precompute q'[0] (Montgomery -N^{-1} mod 2^w), R^2 mod N, and all modulus limbs as circuit CONSTANTS — no in-circuit inverse or per-op setup.
CIOS/Montgomery with carry elimination: when the top modulus word is bounded ((D-1)/2-1), the t[N]/t[N+1] carries are provably zero, dropping ~5N+2 additions per multiply (gnark result).
Limb count sweet spot N<=12 wide limbs; minimize the number of carries that need range checks — each naive range check costs ~1/2 constraint per bit, so wider limbs with fewer carries win.
CRT / RNS residue representation to split the 4096-bit reduce into independent smaller-modulus channels; recombine once at the end.
Only range-check the modular residual, the quotient coefficient, and carries — not every intermediate; use top-bit-fold range checks.

LAZY REDUCTION with static limb-bound tracking (xJsnark long-integer arithmetic): carry a compile-time upper bound per limb and let partial products accumulate in wider limbs; emit a carry-normalization + range check ONLY when a limb's tracked bound would exceed field capacity, instead of normalizing after every op. Across the 16 squarings + 1 multiply this removes whole normalization passes, not just individual carries.

DEFERRAL BUDGET, concretely (circom-ecdsa): with n-bit limbs and k of them, unreduced accumulation is safe while 3n + log2(2k^2) + eps < (native field bits). Use this inequality to place carry/reduce passes at the LAST legal moment instead of guessing; multiples of the fixed modulus used to reduce are compile-time constants.

SUM-OF-PRODUCTS, ONE REDUCTION (arkworks nonnative mul_without_reduce): keep products unreduced in wide limbs and reduce once per accumulated expression, not per multiply. CAUTION: bellman-bignat [OWWB20] and similar bigint libraries are tuned for constraint DENSITY, not constraint COUNT — do not copy their limb layout without re-costing it against allocations+constraints.

mulmod as ONE polynomial-identity check at a single constant point (gnark/eprint 2025/933): hint quotient q and error/carry limbs e out of circuit, then enforce a(X)b(X) = c(X) + alpha(X)q(X) + (2^B - X)e(X) evaluated at ONE fixed X=2^B — collapses the full limb-by-limb equality into a single rank-1 product plus range checks on q,c,e, instead of one constraint per limb coefficient. Evaluate-at-a-point beats coefficient-matching in this R1CS metric; reuse the same hinted-then-checked shape for all 17 squarings/multiplies.

THE 4-DIM CONSTRUCTION IS THE RIGHT ONE and the extra two lattice dimensions come from NON-DETERMINISTIC ADVICE, not from the curve: hint Q = [s]P and verify a relation, which makes the kernel lattice rank 4 with determinant n and all four coefficients about n^(1/4). GENERAL LAW, matching gnark-crypto's own documented bounds to within half a bit: allowing t points in the verified relation gives rank 2t, determinant n^(t-1), coefficients Theta(n^((t-1)/(2t))) — 1.15*sqrt(r) at t=1, 1.25*r^(1/4) at t=2, 1.28*r^(1/3) at t=3. CRUCIALLY THAT EXPONENT INCREASES WITH t, so beyond 4 dimensions the loop gets LONGER: measured 6-dim costs 370251 against 4-dim's 256287, plus about 80k more precomputation — a 70% loss. Per-iteration cost is nearly FLAT in dimension (3727/3810/4104 rows per iteration at 2/4/6 dims), so in-circuit cost is essentially iterations x constant and iterations = bit length. THREE MEASURED NEGATIVES AND TWO SAFETY NOTES FOR THE GLV PATH. (a) j-INVARIANT 0 / a = 0 BUYS EXACTLY ZERO ROWS: compiling the identical gadget for secp256k1 (a=0) and P-256 (a=-3) gives affine add 3345 and affine double 3427 for BOTH, to the row — in software a=0 saves one field addition, and in R1CS a field addition is free. Do not expect anything from the CM structure here. (b) BASE-3 / BASE-(1-omega) EXPANSIONS LOSE: triple costs 4975 against double 3427, so a radix-3 step is 4975 + 3345 = 8320 per log2(3) = 1.585 bits = 5249 rows per bit, against doubleAndAdd at 4896. Note also that omega is a UNIT in Z[omega], so there is no omega-adic expansion at all — only (1-omega), of norm 3 — which is why the Koblitz tau-adic analogy does not transfer and there is no cheap halving. (c) THE DECOMPOSITION PROOF IS NOT WORTH OPTIMISING: it is 1609 rows at 2 dims and 3196 at 4 dims out of 288k-453k, i.e. 0.4% to 1.1%. (ii) IF YOU IMPLEMENT FAKE GLV, THE ALL-ZEROS GUARD IS LOAD-BEARING: assert NOT (v1 = 0 AND v2 = 0), or a malicious hint makes the verified relation vacuous and ANY point Q passes. gnark also had CVE-2025-58157 in this code path (half-GCD non-convergence on negative scalars).

MEASURED TARGET FOR THE MODMUL: 845 SCORE, AGAINST OUR 1463 (mulModSub2Cost = 728 alloc + 735 constr). These numbers come from actually compiling circuits with circom 2.2.3 and reading row counts out of the .r1cs with snarkjs, then witness-testing on 508 vectors including the worst case (p-1)^2 — not from a paper. Reference points, as rows + allocations: circom-ecdsa BigMultModP(64,4) = 7707; circom-pairing FpMultiply(43,6) at secp256k1 = 2509; fold with tightened carry parameters at n=32,k=8 = 1527; FOLD + CRT at n=32,k=8 = 845 (424 rows + 421 allocs). THREE INGREDIENTS, IN ORDER OF IMPORTANCE. (1) THE PRODUCT IS ALREADY FREE — the full 256x256 limb product is 2k-1 rows by asserting the limb-polynomial identity at 2k-1 evaluation points (circom-ecdsa's BigMultNoCarry is 7 rows), so 99.8% of a naive BigMultModP is carries and range checks and NO effort should go into the multiplication. (2) THE FOLD IS FREE FOR EVERY MODULUS — reducing the 2k-1 product limbs back to k via precomputed constants 2^(n(k+i)) mod p is a LINEAR COMBINATION, zero rows. FIXED-BASE SELECTOR HAS 61 ROWS OF SLACK PER WINDOW, AND THE ONE-HOT LAYER IS PROVABLY OPTIMAL. NEW RESULT (proved, and verified numerically for w <= 6): the minimum number of R1CS multiplications to build a full 2^w one-hot from w bits is EXACTLY 2^w - w - 1, and it is split-invariant. Upper bound: combining a size-M and a size-N one-hot needs only (M-1)(N-1) products, since the last row and column follow from the fact that the entries sum to 1, which is free. Lower bound: after m multiplications the wires span at most 1 + w + m dimensions while the 2^w one-hot cells are linearly independent, so m >= 2^w - w - 1. Our SelectX.mainX at 342 breaks down as sign XNOR 11, inner 7-bit one-hot 130 (optimal 120), outer 4-bit one-hot 17 (optimal 11), three product arrays 180, final y 4. The 7/4 split is already optimal. THE REAL SLACK: we select THREE 4-limb quantities when we need x, y+, and a ONE-WIRE BORROW SELECTOR — because p1 = p2 = p3 = 2^64 - 1, the canonical limbs of p - y+ are affine in y+'s limbs given a single borrow bit, and that bit is a COMPILE-TIME CONSTANT per table entry, so select it from the same one-hot for 15 multiplications instead of a whole 4-limb array for 60. A SIGNED {+-1}^4 (GLV-SAC) table has T[15-i] = -T[i], so only 8 entries are stored, VarLookup drops from 135 to about 70 per step, AND no entry is the identity, letting the whole ladder use incomplete addition. OFFSET THE CONSTANT TABLE SO NO WINDOW CAN HIT AN EXCEPTIONAL CASE (halo2 fixed-base gadget): define window w's table as M[w][k] = [(k+2)*(2^wbits)^w]G rather than [k*(2^wbits)^w]G. The +2 does two things: k=0 no longer selects the IDENTITY (so no add-with-infinity guard is needed anywhere), and it kills the collision that a +1 offset would leave (k0=7 with k1=0 would both select [8]G, forcing a DOUBLING, which incomplete addition cannot perform). With every selected point guaranteed non-identity and distinct from the accumulator, the ENTIRE ladder can use incomplete/affine addition with NO complete-add guards and no exception branches — pure constraint savings. Correct the accumulated offset inside the LAST window: M[W-1][k] = [k*(2^wbits)^(W-1) - sum_{j<W-1}(2^wbits)^{j+1}]G, itself a compile-time constant, so the correction is FREE.

Base G is FIXED: every window multiple j*(2^{w*i})*G is a COMPILE-TIME CONSTANT — bake the whole comb table into the circuit as constants (zero constraints to build it), unlike the variable-base case.
Comb method: k = sum b_{i} 2^{i}; group bits into d combs of width w so each step is ONE table select + ONE add; fewer adds than plain windowed double-and-add.
Width-w NAF / signed-digit recoding of the scalar so table entries cover +/- multiples, halving table size and generating more zero (skip) positions.

Signed-digit tables cost almost nothing to apply: -P = (x, -y), so the sign bit drives ONE modular negation of y (an affine op), NOT a second multiplexer. So a width-w signed table needs only 2^{w-1} constant entries selected, plus a conditional y-negation — half the select cost of an unsigned width-w table for the same window count.
Constant-table point selection as a multiplexer over field constants: select cost is linear in window size but touches only additions/booleans, no non-native mul.

DEFERRAL BUDGET: keep 3n + log2(2k^2) + eps < 254 (native field bits); that inequality tells you exactly how many unreduced products you may accumulate before a carry/reduce pass is actually required — defer right up to it, not further.

SUM-OF-PRODUCTS, ONE REDUCTION (arkworks nonnative mul_without_reduce, ~2x fewer reductions): accumulate a*b +/- c*d in WIDE UNREDUCED limbs and reduce ONCE at the end. Affine EC formulas are exactly this shape — lambda = (y2-y1)*inv(x2-x1), x3 = lambda^2 - x1 - x2, y3 = lambda*(x1-x3) - y1 — so reduce once PER OUTPUT COORDINATE, never per intermediate product.

COORDINATE-SYSTEM TRAP: in R1CS an inversion costs ~1 allocation + 1 constraint (hint inv as a witness, enforce x*inv = 1), so division is nearly FREE here — the opposite of the software cost model. Jacobian/projective/co-Z formulas (incl. Meloni co-Z ladders at ~11M+5S+23A per scalar bit) exist ONLY to avoid inversion, and pay for it with extra MULTIPLICATIONS — which are the expensive non-native op in-circuit. Prefer plain AFFINE add/double with hinted inverses; do NOT port inversion-free coordinate systems from the ECC literature.

Combine comb sub-scalars as a joint accumulation sharing point doublings/additions (multi-comb), analogous to the joint-MSM trick, so the fixed precompute is amortized across all windows in one add-chain.

Port secp256k1-scalar-mul's GroupedEqXV / MulModTarget non-native machinery (see reference/) if it lowers the per-add Fp mul-mod cost below the current Flex path; competitor csko pushed this challenge to 90041, a large structural gap — a comb-table + incomplete-add rewrite is likely needed, not incremental tweaks.

GLV IS STRICTLY BETTER ON A FIXED BASE — and is missing from this solution's playbook. Decompose k = k1 + k2*lambda (mod n) into two ~128-bit halves. Because the base is FIXED, lambda*G is itself a COMPILE-TIME CONSTANT: unlike the variable-base case there is NO in-circuit endomorphism to evaluate (variable-base pays ~6 constraints for psi(x,y)=(beta*x, y); here it costs ZERO). You get TWO constant comb tables (multiples of G and of lambda*G), both free to build, and run them as a JOINT accumulation sharing every doubling — roughly halving the add/double chain. The only in-circuit cost is checking the decomposition: k1 + k2*lambda = k (mod n) plus range checks on k1,k2 — one non-native relation, not per-bit work.

Push the same idea further: with all tables being compile-time constants there is no table-size penalty for HIGHER-DIMENSIONAL decomposition (GLV-3 via lambda^2, or 4-dimensional GLV). Each extra dimension shortens the sub-scalars (256 -> ~128 -> ~85 -> ~64 bits) and shortens the shared doubling chain proportionally, at the cost only of more CONSTANT tables (free) and a slightly bigger decomposition check. Sweep the dimension and pick the minimum of (doublings + selects + decomposition check).

mLSB-set comb is the standard pairing of comb methods with GLV curves (see the fixed-base comb / GLV-GLS literature) — combine mLSB-set recoding with the two (or more) constant tables rather than treating comb and GLV as alternatives.
gf2-k12-compress-canonical: HARNESS-VERIFIED COST IDENTITY (same as the gf2-sha256 challenge): SCORE = 2 x (MULTIPLICATIVE COMPLEXITY OVER GF(2)), EXACTLY. The field is literally ZMod 2 and isCidentityRowAt restricts every row to `var k - A*B` with A, B affine, so allocations == constraints == AND count and booleanity costs nothing. DO-NOT-TRY that follows: the single-row non-vanishing-multiplier trick (clean#395) CANNOT transfer to this variant — C must be a bare variable, so the output cannot be hidden inside a multiplicand, and affine*affine never reaches degree 3 over GF(2). Baseline 38400 = 2 x 12 x 1600 confirms the identity. This variant is purely an AND-count problem.

GF(2) CHANGES THE COST MODEL: every element IS a bit, so booleanity constraints vanish entirely — the ONLY cost is chi's multiplication. theta/rho/pi/iota are all F2-LINEAR (XOR = addition, rotation = index permutation, round constant = affine offset) and must cost ZERO.
Baseline 38400 = 12 rounds x 1600 bits x (1 alloc + 1 constraint) — exactly ONE multiplication per state bit. Beating it means beating the MULTIPLICATIVE COMPLEXITY of chi, not shaving overhead.

chi over GF(2): chi_i = a_i + a_{i+2} + a_{i+1}*a_{i+2} (since NOT b = 1+b is affine). Per 5-bit row the products are a1a2,a2a3,a3a4,a4a0,a0a1 — 5 products for 5 outputs, each seemingly used once. LOOK FOR: an algebraic identity computing all 5 row outputs with FEWER than 5 multiplications, products shared between adjacent rows/slices, or a change of basis making chi cheaper.
Only 12 rounds (KangarooTwelve), not 24 — half the rounds of keccak-f1600, so per-round savings are worth proportionally more of the total.

FINAL-ROUND TRIM: the last round's chi feeds only the output. Check whether any intermediate there can be left unmaterialized, or whether the output bits can BE the product witnesses rather than separate allocations — allocations are half the score.

An allocation is only needed for a value that a rank-1 product must reference. Any bit expressible as an affine combination of existing witnesses needs NO allocation — over GF(2) that covers all of theta/rho/pi/iota, so the allocation count should equal the MULTIPLICATION count exactly, never more.

MULTIPLICATIVE-COMPLEXITY FLOOR (SAT-solver literature, FSE 2016 'Optimizing S-Box Implementations ... Using SAT Solvers' and eprint 2023/1721 revisit): the Keccak 5-bit chi S-box has a PROVABLY MINIMAL nonlinear-gate count of 5 — implementations with 5 AND/NCT gates are known and SAT-proven optimal. So 5 muls per 5-bit row x 320 rows = 1600 multiplications per round is a HARD FLOOR for the constraint side; do NOT burn effort hunting a 4-multiplication chi row, it does not exist.

THEREFORE the remaining lever is the ALLOCATION side, not the constraint side. Constraints are pinned at 19200 (12 x 1600 products). The score is allocations+constraints = 38400, so any win must come from allocating FEWER than 19200 witnesses. chi_i = a_i + a_{i+2} + a_{i+1}*a_{i+2} is AFFINE in the product, so only the PRODUCT needs a witness — never allocate the chi output itself. Audit for: outputs materialized separately from their product witness, the final round's 1600 outputs (can they BE product witnesses?), and any witness the mechanical dead-variable pass would delete.

Cross-round product reuse is the only other opening: the linear layer (theta/rho/pi) between rounds mixes lanes, so a product from round r is generally NOT reusable in round r+1 — verify this rather than assume it, but expect no win there.

CALIBRATION AGAINST THE BEST PUBLISHED BOOLEAN CIRCUIT (Bristol Fashion sha256, nigelsmart.github.io/MPC-Circuits): that circuit computes EXACTLY this function — one compression call, buffer + chaining state -> next chaining state — in 22573 AND gates (110644 XOR, 1856 INV, total 135073, AND-depth 1607). Over GF(2) an AND is 1 allocation + 1 constraint (confirmed by the k12 baseline 1600 bits x 12 rounds x 2 = 38400), so the record is (score / 2) ANDs — at 44436 that is 22218, already ~355 BELOW the best-known hand-optimized Boolean circuit. Read that as: this challenge is at state-of-the-art in AND-count terms, generic 'reduce the ANDs' restructuring will NOT find easy wins, and any further gain must come from joint Boyar-Peralta-style minimization of the ADDER carry chains (~17-18k of the ANDs are carries; Ch+Maj are only 2 x 32 x 64 = 4096). Measure your candidate in ANDs and compare to (current seed score / 2) before believing it is an improvement; recompute that ratio from YOUR seed rather than trusting a number quoted here, since the record keeps moving.

GF(2): bits are free of booleanity; XOR/rotate/shift are FREE affine combinations. Cost concentrates in (a) AND gates in Ch/Maj and (b) the mod-2^32 ADDITION carry chains, which are NOT linear over GF(2) and usually dominate.

Minimum-AND forms: Ch(e,f,g) = g + e*(f+g) is ONE multiplication. Maj IS ALSO ONE, not two — Maj(a,b,c) = c + (a+c)*(b+c), since (a+c)(b+c) = ab+ac+bc+c over GF(2) (c^2 = c). The factored form a*b + c*(a+b) costs TWO and the symmetric ab+ac+bc costs three; use the (a+c)(b+c) version everywhere. This is the same identity as the full-adder carry maj(a,b,cin), so Maj and every carry bit cost exactly one multiplication each. Maj appears 32 x 64 = 2048 times, so paying two instead of one wastes up to 2048 ANDs = 4096 score.

CORRECTION — CARRY-SAVE IS NOT A WIN OVER GF(2): a full-adder carry is maj(a,b,cin) = ab + cin(a+b) = ONE multiplication, so a 32-bit mod-2^32 addition costs 31 muls (carries c_1..c_31), and a 3:2 compressor row ALSO costs 31. Reducing k addends therefore costs (k-1)*31 either way — carry-save buys DEPTH, not AND-count. Its advantage in large-field R1CS comes from avoiding range checks, which do not exist here. Do NOT restructure the adder tree expecting a win; the lever is FEWER ADDITIONS and SHARED carry subexpressions, not a different tree shape.

A full-adder carry over GF(2) is maj(a,b,cin) = ab + cin(a+b) — ONE multiplication; the sum bit a+b+cin is free. So a 32-bit ripple costs ~32 muls, and a 3:2 compressor costs 32 muls while removing an entire addend.

Baseline 95904 vs record 44784 — a >2x gap, so the record is NOT using a naive per-addend ripple. Assume a carry-save tree plus minimum-AND Ch/Maj, and look for further sharing of carry subexpressions across the 64 rounds.

Reference point: Flock's pinned SHA-256 R1CS encoder is 30,632 allocations + 30,632 constraints = 61,264 interface-normalized — already beaten by the 44784 record, so treat 61k as a floor to clear, not a goal.

MC FLOOR ARITHMETIC (Boyar-Peralta full-adder/half-adder optimality): count the mandatory multiplications. Per round T1 = h+Sigma1(e)+Ch+K+W is 4 adds = 124, Ch = 32, T2 = Sigma0(a)+Maj is 1 add = 31, Maj = 64, a=T1+T2 = 31, e=d+T1 = 31 -> ~313 muls/round x 64 = ~20.0k; message schedule 3 adds x 31 x 48 = ~4.5k; final 8-word add = 248. Naive total ~24.7k muls -> score ~49.5k. The record is 44780, BELOW that — so the record IS sharing work across rounds. Find the sharing; the adder shape alone will not get you there.

Where the sharing must be: (a) Sigma0/Sigma1/sigma0/sigma1 are free affine rotations — never allocate them; (b) K_t is a CONSTANT so h+K_t is affine, folding one whole addend out of T1's chain; (c) adding a constant costs FEWER than 31 muls because carries into known-zero constant bits are determined — specialize the adder per round constant instead of using a generic 32-bit adder; (d) reuse carry bits between the T1 chain and the e=d+T1 / a=T1+T2 adds where operands coincide.

OPTIMAL COUNTERS BEAT FULL-ADDER CHAINS (Boyar-Peralta, 'The Exact Multiplicative Complexity of the Hamming Weight Function'): MC of the Hamming weight of n bits is EXACTLY n - H(n), where H(n) is the Hamming weight of n's binary representation. Multi-operand addition is column-wise Hamming-weight counting, so a k:log(k) COUNTER is the right primitive, not a chain of 3:2 full adders. Check: k=3 gives 3-H(3)=1 (a full adder, 1 AND — consistent); k=7 gives 7-H(7)=4 ANDs for a 7:3 counter, strictly better than chaining full adders over the same 7 bits. SHA-256 sums 5 addends in T1 plus incoming carries, so columns are 5-7 bits deep — build OPTIMAL COUNTERS per column and let carries propagate between columns, rather than adding operands two at a time. This is the standard AND-minimisation technique and is the most likely source of the large structural drops competitors are landing.

EVERY PER-ADDER BOUND IS ALREADY TIGHT, AND AUTOMATED MC SYNTHESIS LOSES BY 20% — two closed doors, stated so no job wastes itself on them. (a) MC(n-bit addition mod 2^n) = n-1 EXACTLY: ripple achieves n-1, and the degree bound MC >= deg-1 forces >= n-1 because the ANF of c_{n-2} contains a0*b0*prod(a_l + b_l) (Boyar-Peralta, TCS 2008; cited by Testa et al. as '32-bit adder = 32 AND is known to be optimum'). (b) MC(Hamming weight of n bits) = n - H(n), achieved by full-adder trees, so column compression is already optimal. (c) Carry-save/Wallace for k operands mod 2^n costs (k-1)(n-1) — IDENTICAL to sequential ripple, not better; column-counter variants are WORSE (5 operands: 4 ANDs/column x 32 = 128 > 124). THE ONE PIECE OF GENUINELY UNCLAIMED GROUND: THE *JOINT* MC OF MULTI-OPERAND MODULAR ADDITION. Every bound above is per-adder. Nobody has proved anything about adding k operands mod 2^32 in one shot. Boyar-Find (arXiv:1407.6169) does not treat adders at all and their best general (n,n) lower bound is 2n-3; the degree bound only forces about 31 against a construction costing (k-1)(n-1).
